transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I feel like I have to keep doing the same checks and routines over and over to make sure my wife is safe, and it’s taking up my whole day. I'm just so exhausted because I can't seem to stop.

Are these repetitive actions primarily driven by intrusive, distressing thoughts or images that you are trying to neutralize, or are they mainly focused on organizing and arranging things in a specific way?

They are definitely driven by terrifying thoughts that I can't get out of my head, like picturing my wife dying because I miscounted her pills or left salt on her plate. I feel completely forced to do these strict checking and counting routines just to quiet those awful thoughts and make sure nothing catastrophic happens to her.
Do you feel that these repetitive checking and counting routines are excessive or unreasonable, even though you feel compelled to perform them?

Logically, I know these routines are completely excessive and irrational, and I try to tell myself that all the time. But the terrifying fear of something catastrophic happening to my wife is just so overwhelming that I feel absolutely compelled to do them anyway, just to be safe.
